w: At 329 metres, Wiezyca is the highest point in all of central and northern Poland - a forested summit some 40km from Gdansk that ancient Slavs once treated as sacred ground. These days the old pagan cult site doubles as a ski slope, with a lift hauling visitors up to the view instead of the gods.
s: Highest peak in the north - once a pagan Slavic altar
_facts: 329m elevation, highest peak of central and northern Poland
object of pagan cult of ancient Slavs
forested summit with ski lift and ski slope, popular tourist area

w: Nicknamed the 'Kashubian Sea', Wdzydze is the biggest of a chain of five linked lakes inside a landscape park in the Tuchola Forest, its islands - one large enough to be inhabited - covering over 150 hectares between them. Local lore holds that brown trout swim its waters, though ichthyologists disagree.
s: The 'Kashubian Sea' - islands, and a disputed trout legend
_facts: known as the Kashubian Sea, Big Water and Szerzawa
part of a chain of linked lakes: Wdzydze, Radolne, Golun, Jelenie, Slupinko
whole lake part of the Wdzydze Landscape Park
